thread:
Nina (Marketing): hi folks — quick ask for a micro bench we can quote in next week's launch mailer + a short webinar slide. need a reproducible sanity pack to validate two claims: (A) q4_0 quant improves coldstart throughput vs fp16, (B) end-to-end 95p latency <120ms for "short" prompts on redwood-7b-family. can runtime run a small A/B sweep and drop artifacts? preferably single-run, single-host. deadline: Thu EOD. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Tom (Runtime): sounds doable. how small is "small"? 20 prompts? 50? and do you want both coldstart-only and a 5-request warmup series?

Nina (Marketing): 30 short prompts is fine (we'll attach the seed file). Run coldstart (first request post load) + 5-request warmup for the same prompt set. 2 configs: redwood-7b-v2 (fp16) baseline and redwood-7b-v2-q4_0. 2 repeats each. single GPU host.

Priya (EngRuntime): noted. we'll capture raw per-request latencies, 50/95/99 percentiles, and a simple CSV of all samples. want token-level timing? that adds overhead but we can do it if marketing wants to call it out.

Nina (Marketing): token-level is optional — only per-request latencies + percentiles required. include runtime metadata (image tag, model build id, region, instance type). also pin the quant profile string.

Diego (Product): also please log model sha and quant-toolchain version. marketing will include a short caveat line if needed.

Tom (Runtime): ok. we'll run with gpu affinity and single-host runner. sample prompts please paste here or attach. also confirm concurrency: serial invocations (no parallel requests) to measure pure per-request latency?

Nina (Marketing): serial, yes. here's the sample pack (first 6 of 30 shown):
```json
["Explain in one sentence: what is prefix caching?",
 "Short tip: reduce latency for user-facing chat widgets",
 "List 2 tradeoffs of 4-bit quantization",
 "Summarize: why warmup helps with tail latency",
 "How to measure coldstart for tiny prompts",
 "Short reply: best prompt length for <100ms"]
```
(full 30-file attached to the ticket)

benchbot: create_job id=mini-bench-4312345678 runner=single-host-gpu concurrency=1 repeat=2 configs=[fp16,q4_0] est_time=35m

Tom (Runtime): running now. command (for records):
```bash
./run_bench --model redwood-7b-v2-q4_0 --profile q4_0 --prompts prompts_30.json --repeats 2 --serial --capture raw,percentiles,meta --output /tmp/mini-bench-4312345678
```
Will tar artifacts and upload when done.

Priya (EngRuntime): note: we saw a noisy host yesterday in the pool — pinned a clean host tag to avoid background noise. also disabling prefetch to make coldstart measurements deterministic.

Nina (Marketing): great attention to detail, thanks. please surface any anomalies. if variance >12% across repeats, flag and we'll consider a rerun.

benchbot: job mini-bench-4312345678 started at 2026-10-02T14:12:03Z

benchbot: job mini-bench-4312345678 completed at 2026-10-02T14:49:11Z; artifacts uploaded: https://redwood-internal/artifacts/mini-bench-4312345678 (raw_latencies.csv, percentiles.csv, run_manifest.txt, NOTES.md)

Tom (Runtime): uploaded summary CSV + README. quick summary: fp16 95p = 115ms, q4_0 95p = 102ms; coldstart throughput (tokens/sec) improved ~18% on q4_0 for these short prompts. attaching caveats in NOTES.md (sample size, single-host, serial invocations).

Priya (EngRuntime): added runtime metadata: docker:redwood/runtime:2026-10-02-7a3c, model-sha: 9f3a2b, quant-tool: qtool-1.4. Also flagged one outlier in run 2 of fp16 (investigating) — from GPU thermal throttle event, removed before summary.

Nina (Marketing): perfect — downloading artifacts now. can you also drop a 1-paragraph blurb we can lift for the blog and a 1-sentence caveat for the slide?

Tom (Runtime): sure — pushing a tiny text file to the artifact bundle: marketing_blurb.txt and slide_caveat.txt.

benchbot: marketing_blurb.txt and slide_caveat.txt added to artifacts.

Nina (Marketing): you're heroes! :rocket: will follow up if we need a longer warmup rerun for the webinar demo.
